question.text: What will France's provisional year-on-year CPI inflation be for November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: Resolves to the year-on-year change in the French national consumer price index (IPC, "ensemble des ménages", France entière) for November 2026, as stated in the headline of INSEE's provisional estimate release "Consumer price index – provisional results – November 2026" (Informations rapides), scheduled for publication on insee.fr on 27 November 2026 at 08:45 CET (the preceding October 2026 provisional release, which announces that publication date, is at https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/9107975). The value is the year-on-year percentage figure given in that release's title — e.g., a headline reading "In November 2026, consumer prices should increase by 3.6% year on year" resolves as 3.6. The figure as first published governs; INSEE's later revision in its definitive November release (scheduled for 11 December 2026) does not change the resolution. If the provisional release is unavailable, the same INSEE figure as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: The resolved figure is the IPC ("ensemble") year-on-year change, not the harmonised index (IPCH) year-on-year change and not the month-on-month change, both of which are reported in the same release.

research:
I have the data I need and am now writing up the findings.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-30: INSEE's provisional October release (the URL given in the question) shows CPI at +3.4% year on year, after +3.1% in September, and +0.4% month on month. HICP was +3.8% year on year. By component: energy +24.1%, services +2.7%, food +1.2% (fresh food +8.0%), manufactured goods −0.2%, tobacco +3.3%. It confirms the provisional November release for **27 Nov 2026, 08:45**. [INSEE](https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/9107975)
- The same release shows the November 2025 base: CPI was **−0.2% month on month** (definitive) and +0.9% year on year. Rough arithmetic: if November 2026 is flat month on month, the year-on-year rate rises to about 3.6%. Each 0.1 pt of monthly change shifts it by about 0.1 pt. [INSEE](https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/9107975)
- 2026-11-13: The definitive October figure was 3.4%, matching the provisional one (per news reports). The French INSEE page I fetched still showed the provisional text. [cbnews](https://www.cbnews.fr/etudes/inflation-bien-atteint-34-an-octobre-insee)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The figure comes out on 27 November.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Fuel prices tracked by a private site, 1-16 November average compared with October average:
  - diesel €2.214/L vs €2.370 (**−6.6%**)
  - SP95-E10 €2.048 vs €2.155 (**−5.0%**)
  - SP95 €2.118 vs €2.214 (−4.3%)
  - SP98 €2.165 vs €2.266 (−4.5%)

  [mon-carburant](https://mon-carburant.com/prix-moyen-carburant-france/)
- 2026-11-13: Diesel averaged €2.172/L, still falling. 519 stations reported running out of diesel (798 on 9 November). [prix-du-carburant](https://prix-du-carburant.com/actualites/prix-carburants-13-novembre-2026/)
- 2026-11-11: A weekly bulletin put the 30-day trend at diesel −13.5 c/L and SP95 −9.4 c/L. [carburantiq](https://carburantiq.fr/actualites/barometre-prix-carburant-2026-s46) (the page itself returned a 503 error; this figure comes from the search snippet)
- 2026-11-15: Michel-Édouard Leclerc (E.Leclerc) expects inflation of about 4% by early 2027 but stable supermarket prices over Christmas. [capital](https://www.capital.fr/conso/prix-des-courses-michel-edouard-leclerc-annonce-une-mauvaise-nouvelle-pour-2027-mais-une-bonne-pour-noel-1531864)
- 2026-11-01: The regulated benchmark gas price rose 6.6% month on month. The next rise (+5.8%) comes on 1 December, after the November reference period. [service-public](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/actualites/A17956?lang=en)
- How these might add up (my rough calculation, not INSEE's): petroleum products are about 4% of the CPI basket, so a ~5% fall would take roughly −0.2 pt off the monthly change. The gas rise might add about +0.05 to +0.1 pt.

## 4. Base rates
- Recent prints: Jan +0.3, Feb +0.9, Mar +1.7, Aug +2.4, Sep +3.0p / 3.1d, Oct +3.4 (p and d). The year-on-year rate rose 0.3-0.4 pt a month from August to October. [INSEE](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9107965)
- November is seasonally weak, and month-on-month changes have usually been at or below zero:
  - Nov 2025: −0.1 provisional, −0.2 definitive; services fell (transport, communications); energy year on year improved from −5.6% to −4.6%, which suggests energy rose month on month. [INSEE](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/8672062)
  - Nov 2024: about −0.1 (1.3% year on year)
  - Nov 2023: −0.2 (3.5%)
  - Nov 2022: +0.2 (6.2%)
  - Nov 2021: +0.4 (2.8%)
  - The 2021-2024 figures are from my memory, not checked against INSEE.
- What this means:
  - November 2026 fuel prices are falling while they seem to have risen in November 2025, so the base works against energy inflation this month. The opposite was true in August-October.
  - If November 2026 shows the usual seasonal drop of about −0.2 plus the fuel effect, the year-on-year rate would be flat to slightly lower than October's 3.4%.
  - If the monthly change is about 0.0, the rate would be about 3.6%.
- Provisional vs definitive gaps in 2025-26 have been 0 to 0.1 pt.

## 5. Other forecasts
- **The Kalshi "CPI YoY in November" markets in the brief appear to be US CPI, not French.** They sit alongside US "CPI-U index" and "Core CPI" series, and Kalshi labels its French contracts "France inflation rate YoY". They should not be used for this question. [search](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxcpindex/cpiu-index-in-month/kxcpindex-26oct14)
- I found no French November 2026 market on Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold.
- 2026-09-10: INSEE's last Note de conjoncture forecast 2.9% year on year for December 2026 (2026 average 2.1%). Actual inflation has already gone past that path. [INSEE](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9050743)
- September 2026: the Banque de France cut its 2026 average forecast to 2.3% because oil was cheaper than expected. [toutsurmesfinances](https://www.toutsurmesfinances.com/actualites/?p=1943)
- I found no consensus forecast from economists for November.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late November: fuel price moves in the second half of the month. The flash estimate is based on partial price collection plus imputation, so late-month prices matter less.
- The diesel shortages and Middle East/Hormuz tensions could turn fuel prices back up.
- Possible INSEE Note de conjoncture in mid-December: after resolution.
- 2026-11-27, 08:45 CET: INSEE provisional November release (the resolution event).
- No weather dependence beyond the usual heating-energy effects. The regulated gas price for November is already fixed.

- **Base effect:** November 2025's month-on-month change was **−0.2%**. So a November 2026 monthly change of −0.2% would keep the year-on-year rate at about **3.4%**. Every 0.1 point above or below that moves the annual rate by about the same amount (rounding aside).

- **Kalshi's France markets:** only April 2026 and Q1 GDP markets appeared, with no November 2026 one.
- **Analysts:** I found no consensus forecast for French CPI in November 2026.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 11 days remain. INSEE publishes the provisional November 2026 estimate on 27 November 2026 at 08:45 CET.

(b) The latest value is October 2026 at +3.4% year on year, provisional on 30 October and confirmed in the definitive release on 13 November. Month on month it was +0.4%.

(c) If prices stay flat month on month in November 2026, the year-on-year rate rises to about 3.6%. This is because the November 2025 base fell 0.2% month on month.

(d) Continuing the August to October trend of +0.3 to +0.4 pt a month gives about 3.7 to 3.8%. That trend was driven by fuel prices rising in each month, and fuel is now falling clearly in November:
- Average pump prices for 1-16 November are 4 to 7% below October's average.
- Mid-month prices are below that half-month average, so the full-month fall may be closer to 6 to 8%.
- With petroleum products at roughly 4 to 4.5% of the basket, that takes about 0.2 to 0.3 pt off the monthly change.
- The 6.6% rise in the regulated benchmark gas price on 1 November adds about +0.1 pt.
- Seasonal November weakness outside energy, mainly services, has typically been about -0.1 to -0.2 pt. Some pass-through of the energy shock into food and services prices may partly offset it.

Net, I expect the monthly change to be around -0.3%, which puts year-on-year inflation at about 3.3%. The range from -0.5% to 0.0% month on month maps to roughly 3.1 to 3.6%. Rounding adds about ±0.1 pt of noise.

(e) Year-on-year inflation has moved 0.3 to 0.6 pt a month recently. November monthly changes historically run from -0.2 to +0.4. Gaps between provisional and definitive figures have been 0 to 0.1 pt.

(f) I found no French November forecast or market:
- The Kalshi "CPI YoY in November" markets, centred on 3.7 to 3.8%, appear to be US CPI and are not usable here.
- INSEE's September forecast of 2.9% for December has already been overtaken by actual inflation.
- The head of E.Leclerc expects about 4% inflation by early 2027.

(g) Low scenario: fuel prices collapse further in the second half of the month as diesel shortages ease. Combined with a sharp seasonal fall in services and fresh food, the monthly change could reach -0.6%, giving about 2.9 to 3.0%.

High scenario: a Hormuz flare-up reverses fuel prices and second-round effects lift services and food strongly. The monthly change would then be about +0.1 to +0.2%, giving 3.7 to 3.9%.
